q_en: Some words ending in ـًا are not the doer or the thing acted on. What are they telling me?
q_ar: كَلِمَاتٌ تَنْتَهِي بِتَنْوِينِ فَتْحٍ وَلَيْسَتْ فَاعِلًا وَلَا مَفْعُولًا بِهِ. مَاذَا تَقُولُ لِي؟
not_yet: Other accusatives of manner and place: the ḥāl you met in Lesson 57 is another way to say “how”.
The numbers from eleven to ninety-nine: Lesson 71.
The full rules for which number takes which form: later.
not_yet_ar: مَنْصُوبَاتٌ أُخْرَى: الْحَالُ فِي الدَّرْسِ ٥٧ طَرِيقَةٌ أُخْرَى لِقَوْلِ «كَيْفَ».
الْأَعْدَادُ مِنْ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ إِلَى تِسْعَةٍ وَتِسْعِينَ: الدَّرْسُ ٧١.
قَوَاعِدُ الْعَدَدِ وَالْمَعْدُودِ كُلُّهَا: فِيمَا بَعْدُ.

slides.head_en: Look: words that say how many, how, why
sents: Ahmad remembered God a great deal.
ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
Ahmad went to the rawḥa, seeking knowledge.
How many books did you read?

lines: Find the words that end in ـًا. Are they the doer? Are they what the verb was done to?
جِدِ الْكَلِمَاتِ الَّتِي تَنْتَهِي بِتَنْوِينِ فَتْحٍ. هَلْ هِيَ الْفَاعِلُ؟ هَلْ هِيَ مَا وَقَعَ عَلَيْهِ الْفِعْلُ؟
Take the word away. Is the sentence still complete? What is missing?
اِحْذِفِ الْكَلِمَةَ. هَلْ تَبْقَى الْجُمْلَةُ تَامَّةً؟ مَاذَا يَنْقُصُهَا؟
Which question does each one answer: how many? how? or why?
عَنْ أَيِّ سُؤَالٍ تُجِيبُ كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ: كَمْ؟ كَيْفَ؟ أَمْ لِمَاذَا؟

slides.head_en: Three accusatives that answer a question

cards.def_ar: اِسْمٌ نَكِرَةٌ مَنْصُوبٌ يُبَيِّنُ مَا يُقْصَدُ.
cards.def_en: says what is counted or in what respect: after a number or كَمْ

cards.def_ar: مَصْدَرٌ مَنْصُوبٌ مِنْ لَفْظِ الْفِعْلِ: يُبَيِّنُ كَمْ وَكَيْفَ.
cards.def_en: the verb’s own noun, accusative: says how much or how often
a noun of feeling or purpose, accusative: says why

slides.note: After twenty and كَمْ: one singular noun in fatḥa. More numbers: Lesson 71.
slides.note_ar: بَعْدَ عِشْرِينَ وَكَمْ: مُفْرَدٌ مَنْصُوبٌ. بَقِيَّةُ الْأَعْدَادِ: الدَّرْسُ ٧١.

rows: He is better than me in character.
She is greater than me in knowledge.
slides.note: The tamyīz answers “in what respect?” (“better” in character, “greater” in knowledge).

slides.head_en: The absolute object: the verb’s own noun
slides.tip: Add كَثِيرًا or a count (ثَلَاثًا، مَرَّتَيْنِ، مَرَّةً) and you say how much or how often.
slides.tip_ar: زِدْ كَثِيرًا أَوْ عَدَدًا (ثَلَاثًا، مَرَّتَيْنِ، مَرَّةً): تَقُولُ كَمْ أَوْ كَيْفَ.

sents: Ahmad praised God with much praise.
The student was patient, with a fine patience.

slides.note: It says the reason for the action: “out of fear”, “in order to seek”. Ask: لِمَاذَا؟ (why?)

items: tamyīz: كِتَابًا says what is counted
absolute object: ذِكْرًا is the verb’s own noun

slides.why: A student writes عِشْرُونَ كِتَابٌ for “twenty books”. Wrong! After twenty, the counted noun is singular and in the accusative: عِشْرُونَ كِتَابًا.
slides.why_ar: كَتَبَ طَالِبٌ «عِشْرُونَ كِتَابٌ». خَطَأٌ! بَعْدَ عِشْرِينَ يَأْتِي الِاسْمُ مُفْرَدًا مَنْصُوبًا: عِشْرُونَ كِتَابًا.

lines: يَٰأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ اذْكُرُواْ اللَّهَ ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا
O you who believe, remember God with much remembrance.

slides.head_en: A verse of the creed: ʿAqīdat al-ʿAwāmm
lines: And now, know that it is obligatory to know:
of what is due to God, twenty attributes.
فَكَمْ مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ بَلَغَ عُمْرُهُ ثَمَانِينَ سَنَةً وَأَكْثَرَ
How many a Muslim has reached eighty years of age and more,
لَمْ يَجِدْ هَذَا الْبَاعِثَ وَلَمْ يَطْرُقْهُ يَوْمًا مِنَ الدَّهْرِ
and never found this stirring, nor did it knock on him for a single day of his life.
Like one who does good deeds to show off to people.
slides.source: Risālat Ādāb Sulūk al-Murīd of Imām ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād

can: I can say that a word ending in ـًا after a number or كَمْ is the tamyīz (what is counted).
I can spot a verb’s own noun with كَثِيرًا or a count (ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا، ثَلَاثًا) and say it tells how much or how often.
I can spot the noun of reason (خَوْفًا، طَلَبًا، ابْتِغَاءَ) and say it tells why.
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقُولَ إِنَّ الْكَلِمَةَ بَعْدَ عِشْرِينَ أَوْ كَمْ هِيَ التَّمْيِيزُ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَعْرِفَ مَصْدَرَ الْفِعْلِ مَعَ كَثِيرًا أَوْ عَدَدٍ وَأَقُولَ إِنَّهُ يُبَيِّنُ كَمْ وَكَيْفَ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَعْرِفَ الْمَفْعُولَ لِأَجْلِهِ (خَوْفًا، طَلَبًا، ابْتِغَاءَ) وَأَقُولَ إِنَّهُ يُبَيِّنُ السَّبَبَ.

sections.name: A
sections.en: A short text: a morning of dhikr. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: بَعْدَ الصَّلَاةِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ وَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا.
After the prayer Ahmad sat in the mosque and remembered God a great deal.
And he said: Glory be to God and praise be to God.
وَسَأَلَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: كَمْ مَرَّةً ذَكَرْتَ اللَّهَ؟
And the Habib asked him: How many times did you remember God?
قَالَ أَحْمَدُ: ذَكَرْتُ اللَّهَ عِشْرِينَ مَرَّةً.
Ahmad said: I remembered God twenty times.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: اُذْكُرِ اللَّهَ خَوْفًا مِنْهُ وَمَحَبَّةً لَهُ.
The Habib said: Remember God out of fear of Him and love for Him.
ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
Then Ahmad went to the rawḥa, seeking knowledge.
وَقَرَأَ هُنَاكَ عِشْرِينَ صَفْحَةً مِنَ الْكِتَابِ.
And there he read twenty pages of the book.
وَرَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ سَعِيدًا، وَقَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ حَمْدًا كَثِيرًا.
And he returned to the house happy, and said to his mother: Praise be to God, much praise.
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults. Children may skip them.

items.en: Put in order: (a) he read twenty pages; (b) he sat in the mosque; (c) he went home.

items.model: سَعِيدًا: a state (ḥāl): he came back happy.

sections.name: L
sections.en: A line from a letter of Imam al-Ḥaddād (Mukātabāt, vol. 1; vowelled for learners): find the object of reason. Words in the line are glossed below it.
sections.teacher_note: The last row is for adults. Children may skip it.

items.ar: الزَّاهِدُ فِي الدُّنْيَا الْمُتَحَقِّقُ بِالْخَشْيَةِ لِلهِ ، الْعَامِلُ بِمَا عَلِمَ ابْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ اللهِ
items.model: Detached from this world, realised in fear of God, acting on what he knows, seeking the face of God.

items.en: Which word is the object of reason? What question does it answer?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ هِيَ الْمَفْعُولُ لِأَجْلِهِ؟ عَنْ أَيِّ سُؤَالٍ تُجِيبُ؟
items.model: ابْتِغَاءَ (seeking): why does he act on what he knows? To seek the face of God.

items.en: What follows ابْتِغَاءَ? Why does وَجْهِ end in ـِ?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا بَعْدَ ابْتِغَاءَ؟ لِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي وَجْهِ بِكَسْرَةٍ؟
items.model: وَجْهِ اللَّهِ: it is the second part of an “of” phrase (iḍāfa), so it is genitive.

items.en: ★ Which word means “who acts on”? What does it tell you about this man?
items.ar_q: ★ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «الَّذِي يَعْمَلُ»؟ مَاذَا تَقُولُ عَنْ هَذَا الرَّجُلِ؟
items.model: الْعَامِلُ: he does what he knows; knowledge and action go together.

sections.name: S

items.en: A student writes this for “the boy read twenty books”. What is wrong with the ending of the last word?
items.ar_q: مَا الْخَطَأُ فِي نِهَايَةِ الْكَلِمَةِ الْأَخِيرَةِ؟
items.model: After twenty the counted noun is singular and accusative: كِتَابًا. (And what was read is accusative too: عِشْرِينَ.)

items.en: A student writes this for “Ahmad remembered God a great deal”. What is wrong?
items.model: The verb’s own noun and its adjective are accusative here: ذِكْرًا كَثِيرًا.

items.en: A student translates this: “Ahmad went three times for knowledge”. What is wrong?
items.model: طَلَبًا says why (seeking), not how often. It means: Ahmad went seeking knowledge.

items.en: A student writes كَمْ مَرَّةٌ. What is wrong?
items.model: After كَمْ the noun is singular and accusative: كَمْ مَرَّةً.

sections.name: AD
sections.en: The Story Strip: lines 1–104
lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.
The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.
ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا.
The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib.
أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ مُسْرِعًا وَجَلَسَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ.
The boy came to the lesson hurrying, and sat facing the qibla.
And the Habib was pleased with him.
ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَصَلَّى عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ثَلَاثًا.
The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ مَرَّتَيْنِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
The boy read the lesson twice, seeking knowledge.
